helpDefault.intro: Customize a design in your browser and download a ready-to-print file. Everything runs on your device — your settings never leave it, and it works offline.
licenses.note.scadpub: This configurator itself. ScadPub publishes OpenSCAD models as static, browser-based configurators; its own source is MIT-licensed and available at the link above. The MIT license covers ScadPub's own code only — the bundled components listed below carry their own terms.
licenses.note.openscad: Renders the models in your browser. OpenSCAD is free software under the GNU GPL v2 (or later); the corresponding source is available at the link above. Its build also statically links further third-party libraries (e.g. CGAL, Boost, Eigen, Manifold, FreeType, HarfBuzz, fontconfig, libzip) under their own licenses — see the OpenSCAD source for those.
licenses.note.liberation: Bundled fallback typeface. Any external font a deployment requires (e.g. a license-restricted profile font) is not bundled and is uploaded by you.
licenses.note.atkinson: ScadPub bundles this (via Fontsource) as the interface's own display typeface, for the app chrome.
helpDefault.s1.title: 1. Pick a design
helpDefault.s1.body: Use the design name in the top bar to switch between the available designs.
helpDefault.s2.title: 2. Make it yours
helpDefault.s2.body:
The **Customize** tab lists what you can change, grouped into sections.

- Drag a slider (or type a number), pick from a dropdown, type text, or flip a switch.
- Tap the small **ⓘ** next to a label for a fuller explanation.
- Click a **section header** to fold or unfold it; some start folded.
- Some settings only appear when another one makes them relevant.
- **Find a setting…** narrows the list as you type. A long form also offers **Jump to section** (the list button beside it) to skip straight to one.
- Some designs keep their advanced settings out of the way at first. If you see **Show all settings (N more)**, that reveals them; the same control then reads **Show essential settings** to put them back.
- Once you've changed something, a strip at the **top** of the tab counts your changes and offers **Reset to defaults** (or, with a preset applied, **Revert** to it).
helpDefault.s3.title: 3. Look around the preview
helpDefault.s3.body: **Drag** to spin the model, **scroll or pinch** to zoom, and **right-drag** (or two fingers) to move it.
helpDefault.s4.title: 4. Keep the preview fresh
helpDefault.s4.body:
With **Live preview** on, the model updates a moment after each change. You'll find the switch under the settings panel on a wide screen, and in the **⋮** menu (top right) on a phone.

For slow designs it pauses itself — press **Update** over the preview when you're ready.
helpDefault.s5.title: 5. Save your settings (presets)
helpDefault.s5.body:
The **Presets** tab lists **Ready-made** starting points and the ones **Saved by you** (kept in this browser).

- **Save** keeps your current settings under a name so you can come back to them.
- **Export**/**Import** move saved presets between devices as a file (the same format the desktop OpenSCAD Customizer uses).
helpDefault.s6.title: 6. Import fonts and drawings
helpDefault.s6.body:
Some designs use a file of yours — a font for lettering, or an SVG drawing. You add each one from the control that needs it, not from a separate upload screen:

- **Fonts** (`.ttf`/`.otf`): choose **Import font…** in a design's font menu; the font then shows there by name for every design.
- **Drawings** (`.svg`): use the drawing control's **Prepare SVG…** to bring one in.
- The **Files** action (top bar, or the **⋮** menu on a phone) is where you **manage** what you've imported — see each file's type and size, remove one, or clear all. You don't import from there.
- Files stay in this browser and come back on your next visit; nothing is uploaded.
helpDefault.s7.title: 7. Download & share
helpDefault.s7.body:
The two buttons over the preview:

- **Download for 3D printing** — get the printable file for your slicer.
- **Share** (**Copy link** where your browser can't share directly) — a link that reopens this exact design with your settings.

**Save image**, for a picture of the preview, is in the top bar — or the **⋮** menu on a phone.

If anything needs a look before you download, a coloured pill appears just above those buttons (“1 issue to review”). Tap it — or Download — to open **Review**, which summarises what you're about to get and what's unresolved. Once the model has rendered you can still choose **Download anyway**; while a render has failed, that stays unavailable.
helpDefault.s8.title: 8. Appearance & info
helpDefault.s8.body: The **sun/moon** button switches between light, dark, and automatic, and the **ⓘ** button lists open-source licenses. Both sit in the top bar on a wide screen, and in the **⋮** menu (top right) on a phone.
helpDefault.s9.title: Troubleshooting
helpDefault.s9.body: If the preview fails or looks wrong, open **Messages** (the bell in the top bar) — the design reports what it didn't like there, and the Log tab has the full technical output.
svgPrep.find.no-viewbox: the drawing has no canvas frame, so its size on the plate can't be judged reliably
svgPrep.hint.no-viewbox: export with a viewBox (most editors do this automatically) so it always scales the same way
svgPrep.find.viewbox-origin: the drawing's canvas doesn't start at the top-left corner, so parts of it can land off the plate (especially with colour regions)
svgPrep.hint.viewbox-origin: the Fix step re-centres the drawing for you
svgPrep.find.no-geometry: nothing to raise — the drawing has no shapes that can become relief
svgPrep.hint.no-geometry: draw filled shapes (rectangles, circles, paths); only shapes can be raised, not text or images
svgPrep.find.text#one: {count} piece of live text — text can't be raised into relief and will disappear
svgPrep.find.text#other: {count} pieces of live text — text can't be raised into relief and will disappear
svgPrep.hint.text: convert the text to outlines in your editor (Inkscape: Object to Path; Illustrator: Create Outlines), or add wording through the design's own label field instead
svgPrep.find.stroke-only#one: {count} outline-only shape (a stroke with no fill) — every shape is raised as a filled shape, so it comes out solid instead of as a thin outline
svgPrep.find.stroke-only#other: {count} outline-only shapes (a stroke with no fill) — every shape is raised as a filled shape, so these come out solid instead of as thin outlines
svgPrep.hint.stroke-only: give the shape a fill, or convert its outline to a filled shape (Inkscape: Stroke to Path; Illustrator: Outline Stroke) to keep a thin wall or outline
svgPrep.find.open-paths#one: {count} unclosed path — an open path may come out as a thin sliver or not at all
svgPrep.find.open-paths#other: {count} unclosed paths — an open path may come out as a thin sliver or not at all
svgPrep.hint.open-paths: close every path in your editor
svgPrep.find.covers-canvas#one: {count} shape covers the whole canvas — a full-canvas background is raised as one solid block that buries everything on top of it
svgPrep.find.covers-canvas#other: {count} shapes cover the whole canvas — a full-canvas background is raised as one solid block that buries everything on top of it
svgPrep.hint.covers-canvas: remove the background/artboard rectangle (the Fix step drops it); a tactile relief needs open space around the raised shapes
svgPrep.find.active-content#one: {count} element carrying scripts, animation or external references ({names}) — none of it is raised into relief
svgPrep.find.active-content#other: {count} elements carrying scripts, animation or external references ({names}) — none of it is raised into relief
svgPrep.hint.active-content: the Fix step removes them; the shapes and their colours are unaffected
svgPrep.find.ignored#one: {count} <{tag}> element — it isn't supported and won't be raised
svgPrep.find.ignored#other: {count} <{tag}> elements — these aren't supported and won't be raised
svgPrep.hint.ignored: flatten or expand them into plain filled shapes if they carry artwork you need
svgPrep.find.styled-fill#one: {count} shape gets its colour from a stylesheet, which isn't read here — that region is treated as black
svgPrep.find.styled-fill#other: {count} shapes get their colour from a stylesheet, which isn't read here — those regions are treated as black
svgPrep.hint.styled-fill: give each shape a direct fill colour, or a simple class / id / tag colour rule the Fix step can resolve
svgPrep.find.inkscape-trap#one: Inkscape layer name won't be matched as a colour region yet: {names}
svgPrep.find.inkscape-trap#other: Inkscape layer names won't be matched as colour regions yet: {names}
svgPrep.hint.inkscape-trap: the Fix step renames each layer so its name is used as the region, or set an explicit name on the group
svgPrep.find.too-many-regions: {count} colour regions — more than {max} tends to print unreliably, as small regions merge or drop out
svgPrep.hint.too-many-regions: merge the regions that don't need to differ in colour or height
svgPrep.find.shapes-outside-regions#one: {count} shape sits outside every colour region — it imports, but carries no region colour or height of its own
svgPrep.find.shapes-outside-regions#othe: {count} shapes sit outside every colour region — they import, but carry no region colour or height of their own
svgPrep.hint.shapes-outside-regions: move them into one of the named groups, or accept the design's default relief
svgPrep.find.region-is-label: the colour region "{name}" is an Inkscape layer name that won't be matched as-is
svgPrep.hint.region-is-label: the Fix step makes the layer name usable as a region
svgPrep.find.region-missing: no region named "{name}" in the drawing; available: {available}
svgPrep.hint.region-missing: group the shapes for this colour and name the group "{name}" (Inkscape: Object Properties; Illustrator: the layer name)
svgPrep.find.content-outside-viewbox: some artwork sits outside the canvas — it may be cut off
svgPrep.hint.content-outside-viewbox: move everything inside the canvas frame
svgPrep.find.undersized: the drawing fills less than half its canvas — it may come out small and, with colour regions, off-centre
svgPrep.hint.undersized: draw the artwork out to the edges of the canvas
svgPrep.change.layer-kept: left layer "{label}" as-is (another region already uses that name)
svgPrep.change.layer-usable: made layer "{label}" usable as a colour region
svgPrep.change.layer-renamed: made layer "{label}" usable as a colour region, named "{target}"
svgPrep.change.recentred: re-centred the drawing so it sits on the plate
svgPrep.change.removed-background#one: removed {count} full-canvas background that would bury the artwork in one solid block
svgPrep.change.removed-background#other: removed {count} full-canvas backgrounds that would bury the artwork in one solid block
svgPrep.change.removed-external#one: removed {count} external reference from the drawing's styles
svgPrep.change.removed-external#other: removed {count} external references from the drawing's styles
svgPrep.change.removed-unsafe-attrs#one: removed {count} unsafe attribute (event handler or external reference)
svgPrep.change.removed-unsafe-attrs#othe: removed {count} unsafe attributes (event handlers or external references)
svgPrep.change.removed-unsafe-style#one: removed {count} <style> block this module could not vouch for (a disguised or otherwise unsafe reference)
svgPrep.change.removed-unsafe-style#othe: removed {count} <style> blocks this module could not vouch for (a disguised or otherwise unsafe reference)
svgPrep.change.style-fills#one: applied {count} stylesheet colour directly to the shapes
svgPrep.change.style-fills#other: applied {count} stylesheet colours directly to the shapes
svgPrep.change.grouped-colour#one: grouped {count} shape into the "{color}" colour region
svgPrep.change.grouped-colour#other: grouped {count} shapes into the "{color}" colour region
svgPrep.group.no-shapes: Group by colour: no shapes to group
svgPrep.group.transformed: Group by colour: some shapes are transformed or clipped, so regrouping could move them — group them by colour in your editor instead
svgPrep.prepError.spec-separator: region {field} "{value}" contains "," or ":", which separate entries in the layers spec
